title: Lineage change list, format v0
description: What changed between two states of one document. Produced by the Lineage engine and consumed by any tool. Public API: see spec/format/README.md for versioning rules.

specVersion.description: Version of this format. Always "0" in v0.

format.description: Document format the change list describes. v0 covers Word only.

changeId.description: Stable identifier for one change within its change list.

text.description: Text content, or null where the side does not exist (nothing before an insert, nothing after a delete).

kind.description: insert, delete and modify change content; move relocates content (before and after differ if it was also edited); format changes only formatting.

fromLocation.description: Where moved content came from. Required for, and only allowed on, move.

formattingOnly.description: True when the change touches formatting but not content. Shown separately from content changes.

confidence.description: How sure the engine is that this change is mapped correctly, as a whole percentage. Integer on purpose: no floats in the format.

summary.description: Plain-English summary for people, for example "'Data engineer' changed to 'Senior data engineer'".

location.description: Where a change is, keyed by format. Each format adds its own shape in later versions.

part.description: Package part holding the content, for example word/document.xml or word/footnotes.xml.

blockIndex.description: Zero-based index of the block (paragraph, table or section break) in the part.

blockAnchor.description: Optional stable anchor for the block, such as a paragraph ID, that survives moves.

cellLocation.description: A place inside the table at blockIndex: a row, then optionally a column and the block inside that cell. Nested tables nest another cell. A row without a column means the whole row.

blockIndex.description: Zero-based index of the block inside the cell.

charRange.description: Half-open range of characters within the block's text, counted in Unicode scalar values.
